title: Objects, Collections, and a Progress Tracker
summary: Apply arrays, objects, Map, Set, destructuring, immutable updates, and modular design in a progress-tracker capstone.

Test behavior using observable output and assertions

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Arrays represent ordered sequences. Plain objects are effective records with string or symbol property keys. `Map` supports keys of any type and predictable iteration, while `Set` stores unique values. Destructuring extracts named fields and spread syntax can create shallow copies for immutable updates. A shallow copy does not clone nested objects, so update nested state deliberately. Check own properties with `Object.hasOwn` when inherited names must not count. Separate input/output from domain functions so progress calculations can be tested without a browser. Persisted JSON cannot represent functions, Map, Set, `undefined`, or circular references directly.
commonMistakes: passing null does not activate a default parameter
spread creates only a shallow copy

sections.content:

2. Predict each output.
3. Run it in Node.js or a browser console.
4. Change one value.
5. Explain the observed change.
6. Add an assertion for the intended behavior.
